title: Review of Fraudulent Credit Card Transactions Involving Diversion of One-time Passwords Prior to September 2020
what_it_is: Review of Fraudulent Credit Card Transactions Involving Diversion of One-time Passwords Prior to September 2020

sections.label: Affected bank customers and SMS OTP diversion
sections.summary: Banks waived about S$500,000 for 75 affected customers and are reviewing card disputes from September 2020 for SMS OTP diversion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Seventy-five bank customers in Singapore had been affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Banks have reached out to all the affected customers to waive the unauthorised transactions, amounting to approximately S$500,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There have been no confirmed cases of SMS OTP diversion in Singapore prior to September 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Banks are reviewing all card dispute cases reported to them from September 2020, to identify if there may be other fraudulent transactions that were enabled by SMS OTP diversion.

sections.label: SMS OTP diversion case resolution
sections.summary: Banks will waive unauthorised transactions linked to SMS OTP diversion if customers protected their card information and credentials, while the Payments Council reviews guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I emphasise, we are talking about SMS OTP diversion fraud cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have not seen any confirmed cases up to now, prior to September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the banks, as I mentioned just now, are investigating any further reports by consumers and customers, and these will include transactions that occurred before September 2020, taking into consideration this new revelation or this new finding that some of these SMS OTPs could have been diverted and we would take that into consideration in resolving these cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Certainly, if any subsequent report were to be made and found to be linked to SMS OTP diversion, the cases would be resolved as with the 75 cases that I highlighted, which means that for affected customers, the banks will waive the unauthorised transactions, so long as the customers have taken the necessary care to protect their card information and authentication credentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Going forward, for future cases, whether it is due to SMS OTP diversion or other fraudulent methods, I have mentioned before in this House that we have a Payments Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They are reviewing guidelines and responsibilities for customers as well as financial institutions to clarify responsibilities and liabilities.

sections.label: Telcos blocking suspicious SMS diversions
sections.summary: Telcos are putting in place safeguards such as specialised firewalls to monitor and block suspicious SMS diversions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is how, with the compromised credit card credentials, the fraudulent transaction is made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And so, as I mentioned just now, telcos are already putting in place additional safeguards, for example, specialised firewalls and other system safeguards to monitor and block suspicious diversions of SMS.

sections.label: Financial institutions and multi-factor authentication
sections.summary: Financial institutions must implement multi-factor authentication mechanisms, reviewing them continuously according to transaction risk and data sensitivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The financial institutions are required to implement multi-factor authentication mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It can include SMS OTP but they can include other forms of multi-factor authentication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Each one will potentially be susceptible to perpetrators trying to take advantage of any possible weakness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is a continuous process where the financial institutions have to review the type of authentication mechanisms which they would like to use, commensurate with the risk level of the financial transaction and the sensitivity of the data involved.
